sections.name: preroll
sections.note: the 2.000 s poster card: the pad and the logo mnemonic only. No kick, no bass, no hats, no plucks; the first hit is on the cut out of the card

sections.name: lift
sections.note: plucks up an octave, FM index down, shimmer in

sections.name: out
sections.note: single hit, then ring out under the end card, which now holds the spoken close

swells.note: reverse swell into the lift and the end card

bed.padNote: the sustained band-limited chord, voiced two and three octaves above the plucks so it lives in 1-4 kHz - the band a voice rest sounds empty in - without touching the 20-200 Hz anti-engine band.

lines.text: Break is where you make it fail on purpose, without touching the server.
Break a request makes the site fail on purpose, then stops it failing.
A five hundred, a dead connection, a slow reply, or a diverted request.
Submit, and the page says nothing and issues no reference number.
Stop breaking it takes every rule off at once, and the rules stack.
lines.why: all five draws of "Stop breaking it takes every rule off at once, and the rules stack." ended +1.3 to +17.4 ST. Three of the five were inside 3 ST, so the spread is wide and a second set is worth its five tickets.

lines.text: Nothing reloads, and everything the broken requests already put in the session stays.
Stress the layout flips the page right to left and lengthens every label.
Forty per cent longer to start with, the way a translation would be.
Anything that cuts text off is outlined where it happens.
Or whatever Settings says, after you have changed the percentage yourself.
It shows which boxes break when the app is translated, before a translator is hired.
Two tools, and neither needs a server or a translator.

lines.delivery: warm, unhurried, final. Not a sell

voice.note: The commercial's final recipe: one Gemini request per line, one voice and one delivery instruction, the gate selecting by shot fit among contour-passing draws, the clean chain with a +6 dB bell at 3.9 kHz whose gain is inside the voice trim.
